Pepper Bell Bacterial Spot.overview: Bacterial spot causes water-soaked angular leaf spots, premature defoliation, and rough scabby fruit lesions.
Pepper Bell Bacterial Spot.symptoms: Small circular-to-angular dark spots with yellow halos; leaf drop; sunken scabs on fruit.
Pepper Bell Bacterial Spot.causes: Splashing rain, overhead irrigation, contaminated seed, and high humidity (> 80%).
Pepper Bell Bacterial Spot.treatment: Copper Hydroxide (2 g/L) tank-mixed with Mancozeb (2 g/L). Apply early morning.
Pepper Bell Bacterial Spot.prevention: Use certified seeds, install drip irrigation, and maintain 2-year non-host rotation.
Pepper Bell Bacterial Spot.fertilizer: Balanced NPK (1:1:2); avoid high nitrogen which forces soft, vulnerable growth.
Pepper Bell Bacterial Spot.pest_control: Control thrips and flea beetles to prevent entry wounds.
Pepper Bell Bacterial Spot.farmer_tips: Prune lower leaves up to 15 cm above ground during a dry afternoon.

Pepper Bell Healthy.overview: Foliage exhibits vigorous chlorophyll pigmentation, balanced cellular turgor, and zero pathogen marks.
Pepper Bell Healthy.symptoms: Uniform deep green color, intact margins, and robust apical shoot growth.
Pepper Bell Healthy.causes: Optimal soil moisture, balanced fertilization, and adequate sun exposure.
Pepper Bell Healthy.prevention: Weekly scouting, organic straw mulching, and routine bed hygiene.
Pepper Bell Healthy.fertilizer: Apply balanced organic compost and maintain adequate calcium.
Pepper Bell Healthy.pest_control: Deploy yellow sticky traps for aphids and whiteflies.
Pepper Bell Healthy.farmer_tips: Ensure soil stays moist but well-drained to avoid flower drop.

Potato Early Blight.overview: Causes concentric target-board lesions on older leaves, reducing photosynthesis and tuber yield.
Potato Early Blight.symptoms: Dark brown circular spots with concentric rings and yellow chlorotic halos on lower leaves.
Potato Early Blight.causes: Alternating wet and dry cycles, plant stress, and overwintering spores in soil debris.
Potato Early Blight.treatment: Chlorothalonil (2 g/L) or Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole (1 ml/L).
Potato Early Blight.prevention: 3-year crop rotation, hill up soil over tubers, and avoid late-afternoon irrigation.
Potato Early Blight.fertilizer: Ensure sufficient potassium and balanced micronutrients.
Potato Early Blight.pest_control: Control potato beetles and flea beetles.
Potato Early Blight.farmer_tips: Strip infected lower foliage as soon as spots appear.

Potato Healthy.overview: Potato foliage demonstrates active vegetative growth, strong vascular stems, and clean stolons.
Potato Healthy.symptoms: Lush green foliage, uniform leaf margins, and absence of lesions.
Potato Healthy.causes: Certified seed tubers, loose sandy loam, and balanced moisture.
Potato Healthy.prevention: Hill up soil regularly and avoid prolonged foliar wetness.
Potato Healthy.fertilizer: Apply phosphorus and potassium-rich fertilizers during tuber bulking.
Potato Healthy.pest_control: Monitor leaf undersides for green peach aphids.
Potato Healthy.farmer_tips: Stop nitrogen feeding 3 weeks prior to harvest for skin set.

Potato Late Blight.overview: Destructive water-mold disease that rapidly rots leaves, stems, and stored tubers in cool, wet weather.
Potato Late Blight.symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions with white downy mold on leaf undersides; greasy brown stem cankers.
Potato Late Blight.causes: Temperatures 10-21°C, relative humidity > 90%, and prolonged rain or heavy fog.
Potato Late Blight.treatment: Dimethomorph (1 g/L), Cymoxanil + Mancozeb (2.5 g/L), or Mandipropamid (0.8 ml/L).
Potato Late Blight.prevention: Plant certified seed tubers, eliminate cull piles, and monitor regional blight alerts.
Potato Late Blight.fertilizer: Avoid excess nitrogen which promotes dense canopies.
Potato Late Blight.pest_control: Eradicate wild nightshade weeds around field boundaries.
Potato Late Blight.farmer_tips: Kill vines (desiccate) 2 weeks before digging if blight is present.

Tomato Bacterial Spot.overview: Causes foliar blighting, blossom drop, and rough scab-like spots on tomato fruit.
Tomato Bacterial Spot.symptoms: Small angular dark greasy spots with yellow halos; leaves turn brown and ragged.
Tomato Bacterial Spot.causes: Rain splash, warm temperatures (25-32°C), and infected seed lots.
Tomato Bacterial Spot.prevention: Use pathogen-free certified seed, drip irrigation, and tool disinfection.
Tomato Bacterial Spot.fertilizer: Maintain balanced NPK with soil pH between 6.2 and 6.8.
Tomato Bacterial Spot.pest_control: Control stink bugs and leaf-footed bugs.
Tomato Bacterial Spot.farmer_tips: Prune and stake plants to keep foliage off wet soil.

Tomato Early Blight.overview: Causes collar rot, target-like concentric leaf spots, and stem-end fruit rot.
Tomato Early Blight.symptoms: Concentric target rings surrounded by yellow halos starting on lowest leaves.
Tomato Early Blight.causes: Fungal spores splashing from soil debris during rain or overhead watering.
Tomato Early Blight.treatment: Mancozeb (2.5 g/L), Chlorothalonil (2 g/L), or Azoxystrobin (1 ml/L).
Tomato Early Blight.prevention: Mulch soil with organic straw, stake vines, and maintain 3-year rotation.
Tomato Early Blight.fertilizer: Maintain steady potassium and organic compost feeding.
Tomato Early Blight.farmer_tips: Trim lower 30 cm of foliage once plants reach 1 meter height.

Tomato Healthy.overview: Foliage exhibits rich green color, vigorous growth tips, and clean blossom clusters.
Tomato Healthy.symptoms: Uniform deep green leaves, robust stems, and no necrotic lesions.
Tomato Healthy.causes: Balanced watering, fertile loamy soil, and 6-8 hours of direct sunlight.
Tomato Healthy.prevention: Prune non-fruiting suckers and maintain regular scouting.
Tomato Healthy.fertilizer: Feed with low-nitrogen, high-phosphorus/potassium formula during fruiting.
Tomato Healthy.pest_control: Scout weekly for hornworms, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Tomato Healthy.farmer_tips: Water consistently at root level to prevent blossom end rot.

Tomato Late Blight.overview: Rapidly rots green and ripe fruit, turning vines and foliage brown and collapsed.
Tomato Late Blight.symptoms: Irregular water-soaked greasy patches with white fuzzy mold underneath in humidity.
Tomato Late Blight.causes: Cool, wet, overcast weather (12-22°C) with prolonged relative humidity (> 90%).
Tomato Late Blight.treatment: Mandipropamid (0.8 ml/L), Dimethomorph (1 g/L), or Cymoxanil + Mancozeb (2.5 g/L).
Tomato Late Blight.prevention: Plant resistant cultivars, maximize row spacing, and water at ground level.
Tomato Late Blight.fertilizer: Avoid high-nitrogen fertilizers that create dense foliar canopies.
Tomato Late Blight.pest_control: Clear nightshade weeds and volunteer potatoes.
Tomato Late Blight.farmer_tips: Remove and seal infected vines immediately in trash bags.

Tomato Leaf Mold.overview: Greenhouse and polyhouse disease favored by stagnant air and humidity above 85%.
Tomato Leaf Mold.symptoms: Yellow patches on upper leaf surface with olive-brown velvety mold underneath.
Tomato Leaf Mold.causes: Relative humidity > 85% and temperatures 20-25°C in enclosed structures.
Tomato Leaf Mold.treatment: Potassium Bicarbonate (3 g/L) or Copper Hydroxide (2 g/L).
Tomato Leaf Mold.prevention: Run greenhouse ventilation fans overnight and space plants generously.
Tomato Leaf Mold.fertilizer: Ensure adequate calcium and potash to toughen leaf cuticles.
Tomato Leaf Mold.farmer_tips: Prune dense interior foliage to allow sunlight penetration.

Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot.overview: Strips plants of lower leaves, exposing fruit to sunscald and reducing harvest.
Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot.symptoms: Small circular spots (2-3 mm) with dark margins and gray centers containing tiny black dots.
Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot.causes: Overwintering spores in soil debris splashing onto lower leaves during rain.
Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot.treatment: Chlorothalonil (2 g/L), Mancozeb (2.5 g/L), or Copper Octanoate (2.5 ml/L).
Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot.prevention: Mulch soil beds thoroughly, practice 3-year rotation, and use drip irrigation.
Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot.fertilizer: Apply balanced compost tea to reduce defoliation stress.
Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot.farmer_tips: Disinfect tomato cages and stakes between growing seasons.

Tomato Spider Mites.overview: Sap-sucking microscopic mites that cause stippling, chlorosis, and fine webbing.
Tomato Spider Mites.symptoms: Yellow/white stippling dots across leaves, bronzed foliage, and silky webs.
Tomato Spider Mites.causes: Hot, dry, dusty weather (> 28°C) and drought stress.
Tomato Spider Mites.treatment: Abamectin (0.5 ml/L), Spiromesifen (0.8 ml/L), or Neem Oil (4 ml/L).
Tomato Spider Mites.prevention: Keep plants hydrated, dampen dusty farm paths, and preserve predatory mites.
Tomato Spider Mites.fertilizer: Avoid high-nitrogen synthetic feeds which boost mite reproduction.
Tomato Spider Mites.farmer_tips: Spray leaf undersides thoroughly with high-pressure nozzles.

Tomato Target Spot.overview: Causes brown concentric leaf spots and sunken crater-like pits on mature tomato fruit.
Tomato Target Spot.symptoms: Circular brown spots with light centers and concentric rings; sunken fruit pits.
Tomato Target Spot.causes: Warm, humid climates (25-32°C) and poor canopy airflow.
Tomato Target Spot.prevention: Increase row spacing, stake vines upright, and use drip lines.
Tomato Target Spot.fertilizer: Provide consistent calcium and potassium for fruit wall firmness.
Tomato Target Spot.pest_control: Control alternate weed hosts in field borders.
Tomato Target Spot.farmer_tips: Harvest mature green or blushing fruit promptly.

Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.overview: Whitefly-transmitted virus causing severe stunting, upward leaf curling, and flower drop.
Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.symptoms: Upward cupping of leaves, interveinal yellowing, stunted growth, and zero fruit set.
Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.causes: Vectored exclusively by silverleaf whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci).
Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.treatment: No viricide exists. Control whitefly vectors using Imidacloprid (0.5 ml/L) or Pymetrozine (0.6 g/L).
Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids (Tygress, Charger), use 50-mesh netting, and silver mulch.
Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.fertilizer: Maintain healthy soil organic matter to support unaffected plants.
Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.farmer_tips: Immediately rogue out and bag infected plants.

Tomato Mosaic Virus.overview: Mechanically transmitted virus causing mottled foliage, shoestring leaves, and fruit browning.
Tomato Mosaic Virus.symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic pattern on leaves, distorted foliage, and internal fruit browning.
Tomato Mosaic Virus.causes: Physical handling, contaminated pruning shears, infected seed, and tobacco products.
Tomato Mosaic Virus.treatment: No antiviral cure. Remove and burn symptomatic plants.
Tomato Mosaic Virus.prevention: Plant certified mosaic-resistant seed, wash hands with soap, and prohibit tobacco near crops.
Tomato Mosaic Virus.fertilizer: Provide balanced organic feed to strengthen healthy neighboring plants.
Tomato Mosaic Virus.pest_control: Disinfect tools with 20% non-fat dry milk solution or 10% bleach.
Tomato Mosaic Virus.farmer_tips: Work in young, healthy plant blocks before visiting older blocks.

Brinjal Phomopsis Blight.overview: Major disease of brinjal causing collar rot in seedlings, leaf spotting, and fruit rot.
Brinjal Phomopsis Blight.symptoms: Circular brown leaf spots with pycnidia; sunken soft rotting spots on fruit.
Brinjal Phomopsis Blight.causes: Overwinters in crop debris and infected seed; high humidity and warm rains.
Brinjal Phomopsis Blight.treatment: Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Carbendazim (1 g/L) at 10-day intervals.
Brinjal Phomopsis Blight.prevention: Hot-water seed treatment at 50°C for 30 mins; 3-year crop rotation.
Brinjal Phomopsis Blight.fertilizer: Balanced NPK (100:50:50 kg/ha); avoid excess nitrogen.
Brinjal Phomopsis Blight.pest_control: Control shoot and fruit borers (Leucinodes orbonalis).
Brinjal Phomopsis Blight.farmer_tips: Collect and destroy all fallen diseased fruits immediately.

Chilli Anthracnose / Dieback.overview: Causes drying of twigs from top downwards (dieback) and sunken circular lesions on ripe chillies.
Chilli Anthracnose / Dieback.symptoms: Necrotic twigs turning straw-colored; dark concentric sunken spots with pinkish spore masses on fruits.
Chilli Anthracnose / Dieback.causes: Warm rainy weather (28-30°C), high humidity (> 80%), and infected seeds.
Chilli Anthracnose / Dieback.treatment: Azoxystrobin (1 ml/L) or Copper Oxychloride (3 g/L) at flowering stage.
Chilli Anthracnose / Dieback.prevention: Seed treatment with Thiram (2 g/kg); remove infected dead branches.
Chilli Anthracnose / Dieback.fertilizer: Apply potassium sulfate to improve fruit skin thickness.
Chilli Anthracnose / Dieback.pest_control: Manage chilli thrips (Scirtothrips dorsalis) with Spinosad.
Chilli Anthracnose / Dieback.farmer_tips: Harvest mature ripe chillies promptly to prevent fruit rot spread.

Okra Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus.overview: Most damaging viral disease of bhindi, turning leaves yellow and fruits small, hard, and unmarketable.
Okra Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus.symptoms: Network of yellow veins on green background; leaves turn completely yellow; stunted growth.
Okra Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus.causes: Transmitted by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) in warm humid weather.
Okra Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus.treatment: Control whitefly vector: Acetamiprid (0.4 g/L) or Thiamethoxam (0.3 g/L).
Okra Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus.prevention: Grow resistant varieties (Arka Anamika, Parbhani Kranti); rogue out early infected plants.
Okra Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus.fertilizer: Ensure balanced basal fertilization with farmyard manure.
Okra Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus.farmer_tips: Sow barrier crops like maize or sorghum around the okra plot.

Cabbage Black Rot.overview: Bacterial vascular disease causing characteristic V-shaped yellow lesions starting from leaf edges.
Cabbage Black Rot.symptoms: V-shaped chlorotic lesions with black vein network at leaf margins; vascular blackening in stem.
Cabbage Black Rot.causes: Infected seed, warm rains (25-30°C), and water splash through hydathodes.
Cabbage Black Rot.treatment: Copper Hydroxide (2 g/L) + Streptocycline (0.1 g/L) preventative foliar spray.
Cabbage Black Rot.prevention: Hot-water seed soak at 50°C for 30 minutes; 3-year non-crucifer rotation.
Cabbage Black Rot.fertilizer: Avoid excessive nitrogen which promotes soft heading tissue.
Cabbage Black Rot.farmer_tips: Do not cultivate or weed field while leaves are damp.

Cucumber Downy Mildew.overview: Fast-spreading foliar disease causing angular yellow spots bounded by leaf veins.
Cucumber Downy Mildew.symptoms: Angular yellow patches on upper leaf surface; purple-gray fuzzy sporulation on lower surface.
Cucumber Downy Mildew.causes: Cool to warm humid conditions, high dew, and sprinkler irrigation.
Cucumber Downy Mildew.treatment: Cymoxanil + Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Dimethomorph (1 g/L).
Cucumber Downy Mildew.prevention: Trellis vines for aeration, use drip lines, and select tolerant hybrid seeds.
Cucumber Downy Mildew.fertilizer: Maintain balanced potassium and calcium feeding.
Cucumber Downy Mildew.pest_control: Scout for cucumber beetles and aphids.
Cucumber Downy Mildew.farmer_tips: Spray undersides of leaves thoroughly before rain fronts.

Onion Purple Blotch.overview: Causes purple sunken lesions on onion leaves and flower stalks, leading to premature leaf collapse.
Onion Purple Blotch.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots developing purple-brown centers with yellow halos; leaf tips die back.
Onion Purple Blotch.causes: Warm humid weather (25-30°C), heavy dew, and thrips injury.
Onion Purple Blotch.treatment: Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Tebuconazole (1 ml/L) with sticker/spreader.
Onion Purple Blotch.prevention: Good soil drainage, certified seed bulbs, and 3-year crop rotation.
Onion Purple Blotch.fertilizer: Apply balanced sulfur and potassium for bulb skin durability.
Onion Purple Blotch.pest_control: Control onion thrips (Thrips tabaci) with Fipronil (1.5 ml/L).
Onion Purple Blotch.farmer_tips: Always add a surfactant/spreader to sprays because onion leaves have waxy cuticles.

Spinach Downy Mildew.overview: Causes yellow blotches on tender spinach leaves with dense purple-gray mold underneath.
Spinach Downy Mildew.symptoms: Pale yellow chlorotic patches on upper foliage; violet-gray fungal fuzz underneath; leaves curl and rot.
Spinach Downy Mildew.causes: Cool, wet, humid weather (10-18°C) and dense plant stands.
Spinach Downy Mildew.treatment: Copper Octanoate (2.5 ml/L) or Potassium Phosphite (2 ml/L).
Spinach Downy Mildew.prevention: Use resistant spinach varieties, thin plants for airflow, and irrigate in early morning.
Spinach Downy Mildew.fertilizer: Apply balanced organic compost; avoid high foliar nitrogen.
Spinach Downy Mildew.pest_control: Manage leaf miners with neem formulations.
Spinach Downy Mildew.farmer_tips: Harvest uninfected leaves early if disease pressure is rising.

French Bean Rust.overview: Fungal rust producing reddish-brown powdery pustules on leaves, causing premature defoliation.
French Bean Rust.symptoms: Small raised reddish-brown powdery pustules surrounded by yellow halos on leaf undersides.
French Bean Rust.causes: Moderate temperatures (18-25°C), high humidity (> 95%), and extended leaf moisture.
French Bean Rust.treatment: Wettable Sulfur (3 g/L) or Hexaconazole (1 ml/L) at first pustule appearance.
French Bean Rust.prevention: Plant resistant cultivars, wide row spacing, and clean crop residue post-harvest.
French Bean Rust.fertilizer: Ensure adequate phosphorus and potassium; avoid excess nitrogen.
French Bean Rust.farmer_tips: Avoid touching wet bean foliage during harvesting.

Cauliflower Downy Mildew.overview: Attacks seedlings and mature curd foliage, causing yellow spots and gray downy mold.
Cauliflower Downy Mildew.symptoms: Yellow angular leaf spots on upper surface; white downy growth underneath; curd browning.
Cauliflower Downy Mildew.causes: Cool foggy weather (10-18°C) and heavy morning dew.
Cauliflower Downy Mildew.treatment: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Dimethomorph (1 g/L).
Cauliflower Downy Mildew.prevention: Seed treatment with Thiram; nursery raised beds with good drainage.
Cauliflower Downy Mildew.fertilizer: Supplement with Boron (Borax @ 10 kg/ha) to prevent curd browning.
Cauliflower Downy Mildew.pest_control: Scout for aphids and cabbage loopers.
Cauliflower Downy Mildew.farmer_tips: Ensure nursery beds are not overcrowded.
